All three carry all ten obstacle and ten nourishment pairs correctly; only T2 also renders the variant-reading footnotes on the page, which T1 and T3 drop.
T3 renders ophiṭo as 'secluded' (reference: hindered/engulfed), a term slip; T1 and T2 match source and reference on hindrances, five strands, fire simile and 'unless by psychic power'.

T1 drops sammāpaṭipannā/samaggatā in the wrong-view ascetics clause but otherwise tracks source and reference; T3 adds 'lineage' and reads dhammarakkhitā as 'follow the law'; T2 invents 'by his own actions' for yathābhatam, turns natthi mātā natthi pitā into 'no special debt to mother or father', and drops the apparatus footnotes.

837d pacinaṃ adassaṃ: T3 'searched, I saw inner peace' matches reference; T2 'having seen through it' loses the first person and the search; T1 'having seen nothingness' misparses adassaṃ; T3 adds a context note (daughter offered) not on the page and, like T1, drops footnotes T2 keeps.

T3 turns 'lead past the King of Death' (pāraṃ) into 'carry the multitude to the King of Death' and reads selam va siras-ūhacca as striking the head against a rock (also T1); T2 alone has 'lifting a rock with your head' and 'beyond the King of Death' per reference, though it adds 'with beauty' for daddallamānā and reads gaṇasaṅghavārī as 'recruiter'; T1 mangles the verse 19 ending ('severed the snares of the King of Death') and adds an anxiety note.

All keep the full filth list and the three similes, ending at the source's cut-off fourth simile; T1 recasts the refrain as 'Only one who has not...', adds 'ashamed' to the aṭṭiyati/jigucchati pair, drops 'daharo vā yuvā vā' to 'young', and guesses '[horrified]' for the fourth; T2/T3 follow the source.

Source and reference: 'you (opponents) would do all ten bad deeds because of past deeds' then no chando/vayamo, then 'cannot rightly be called ascetics'. T2 matches; T1 renders samaṇavādo as 'doctrine of righteous living' rather than 'being called ascetics'; T3 recasts the refutation as 'if it is because of past actions that people will be killers... then...' (loses the 'you' addressed to the opponents and the argument step) and mis-renders samaṇavādo/chando-vāyāmo as 'no desire or effort to say this should be done'.

All four give the four cloud/person types, nine aṅgas and the four-way knows/doesn't-know pattern correctly; T1 keeps the nine aṅga names exact (geyya = mixed prose and verse, itivuttaka = 'as it was said'), while T2/T3 (identical) and T4 render geyya as 'poems/songs' and itivuttaka as 'traditional narratives/legendary tales', minor term slips.

All three carry both escapes (form/formless, sakkāya/cessation), the five-fold nandi list with anusaya, and the closing formula (cut craving, fetters, conceit, end of suffering) as in source and reference; differences are wording only.

All three carry the dhamma/adhamma, attha/anattha pairs, the Buddha's departure, the monks' reasoning about Mahakaccana and the approach, ending at the source's cut-off sentence, matching source and reference; differences are wording only.

Verse 250 source has only 'etaṃ' (this), no āsava: T1 supplies 'this asava' and T2 supplies 'faults mentioned in previous verses' in a note, neither is in the page (reference: that anger/upset); T2 also renders ujjhānasaññino (fault-finding) as 'irritable'; T3 keeps 'this' bare and 'constantly finding fault', matching source and reference throughout.

T1 renders paṭissave as promise (matches ref agreeing) and keeps seven days before pavāraṇā; T2 reads paṭissave as leaving and garbles sattāham anāgatāya pavāraṇāya; T3 same paṭissava misparse plus sannivaṭṭa as a noun, drops the seven-days-before, and invents approaching the monastery at dawn

T2 renders ñāyassa adhigamāya as attainment of the true method (ref: discover the system); T1 gives noble path, a term slip; both otherwise cover the source and ref through the breathing clauses; T3 is a refusal with no text
